Title:
[ABC-104] feat(access-rules): define the access rules in-repo and check them against CODEOWNERS

Body:
## Description
Who may merge a change was previously implicit, scattered between institutional knowledge and a design doc outside the repo. This defines it in `docs/access-rules.md` as a path-ordered table, encodes the same table in `CODEOWNERS`, and adds a drift check (`bin/check-access-rules.mjs`) that fails when the two disagree, run in CI on every pull request and on every push to main.

`fixtures/recordings/` and `docker-compose.yml` are called out explicitly rather than left to the table's default, since each already has its own sign-off rule elsewhere; folding them into the default would have tightened who may merge them.

Ruleset enforcement (requiring code-owner review on signature paths) is deliberately left open: the account that currently opens agent-prepared pull requests is also the signing account, and the forge does not let an author approve their own PR. Turning enforcement on now would make every signature-path PR unmergeable. That identity question is tracked separately and unresolved.

## Verification
`node --test bin/check-access-rules.test.mjs` passes: it seeds every drift kind the checker reports (missing or extra pattern, precedence order, an unowned signature path, a signature path owned by someone other than the sign-off team, a duplicate pattern) and confirms each is caught, plus a round-trip check that the committed document and `CODEOWNERS` agree.
